description: SEC-03 (system review 19-10-2026): the harness's own rule files, scored like an F2 sensitive path so an agent cannot quietly switch off the guard that watches it. Read by harness_sensitivity.py next to sensitive-paths.json.
enforcement_note: HONEST STATUS (C10): enforced only where sensitive-paths.json has enforce_at_pretooluse=true (the shipped value), by the PreToolUse guard (PowerShell and bash both call harness_sensitivity.py), for the Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit tools. A shell write is not intercepted, and the guard fails OPEN on any error. Defense-in-depth against an agent steered by injected text, not a boundary against a person.
why_not_on_the_preserve_list: sensitive-paths.json is project-owned (preserve list), so a rule added there never reaches a project that already has the file. This file is bundle-owned: every update replaces it.
skip_note: The toolkit source repo is recognised by shape, as the installer does for B-85: both a bundle manifest and the packer. There, editing these files is the work itself. One half of the shape is not enough.

rules.reason: Harness rule file: a write here can turn the guard off for every later call. Edit it by hand, update it through the bundle, or get the write approved on the Portal.

notes.excluded: casan-policies.yaml and token-pricing.json are project-tuned (on the preserve list) and switch no gate off. .claude/settings.local.json is personal and never shipped, so it is not listed at all.
notes.why_approvable: Same escape hatch as db-migrations: a reviewer on the Portal can approve exactly one write of exactly these bytes. Hard-blocking with no way through would get the whole guard switched off instead.
